title: Adaptive index-hinting and cross-tenant prefetch for wide-range dashboard queries
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Long-running dashboard queries that request large time ranges (30d+) or deep cursor offsets cause high coordinator CPU, unbounded memory spikes in the query router, and frequent index scans that hurt tail latency. Existing fixes (static prefetch windows and coarse shard routing) either overfetch or fail to help multi-tenant queries that span hot and cold partitions.

Goal: Reduce 95th and 99th percentile latency for wide-range dashboard queries by introducing an adaptive index-hinting layer that guides the storage engine to use narrow time-range index seeks, combined with a cross-tenant prefetch mechanism that materializes temporary micro-aggregates for popular wide-range views. The solution should avoid increased load for small/point queries and fall back gracefully under resource pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile query latency improvement >= 2x for >7d range queries on dev cluster (representative load)
No regression (<5%) on P50 for point and recent-range queries
Memory usage of query router under representative load stays below current baseline + 10%
Feature gated and disabled by default; enable flag per-tenant via Console
Automated e2e tests validating index hints correctness and prefetch eviction behavior
Runbook entry created describing fallback behavior and how to disable prefetch per-tenant
design_decisions: Add a lightweight Index Hint Generator in the query router that inspects requested time range cardinality and emits a set of range seeks instead of a single broad scan

Implement a cross-tenant prefetch service (prefetch-daemon) that listens for high-frequency wide-range queries and creates ephemeral micro-aggregates stored in a TTL-backed cache in Redis or a local SSD tier
Use adaptive heuristics: if the requested range intersects >3 disjoint hot shards, prefer index hints; if it spans >30d and query frequency > threshold, trigger prefetch
Graceful degradation: when prefetch cache is saturated, fall back to index hints only; when routing CPU is high, disable hint expansion and revert to existing planner
Expose per-tenant flags: prefetch_enabled, hint_aggressiveness (low/med/high), prefetch_ttl_days
implementation_todos: Prototype Index Hint Generator (router) that transforms a range scan into N seeks (N configurable)
Add planner unit tests and integrate with existing query execution mocks
Build prefetch-daemon service with metric instrumentation (prefetch_hits, prefetch_misses, eviction_rate)
Add persisted per-tenant feature flag in tenant config and Console toggle
Create a middleware to surface prefetch cost estimates in query explain output
Instrument telemetry to correlate prefetch usage with token costs and latency improvements
Create e2e test harness using synthetic multi-tenant workloads (hot/cold shard mixtures)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Lab testing with 3-node dev cluster; verify correctness and unit tests (owner: Liam)
Stage 1: Canary in staging against sampled traffic (enable for 10 tenants with mixed workloads)
Stage 2: Gradual rollout to 5% of production tenants; monitor prefetch cost, latency, eviction_rate
Stage 3: Increase to 25% after two weeks if no regressions; capture cost delta and SLO impact
Stage 4: GA opt-in with Console toggle; default off for new tenants until vetted by SRE and PM
telemetry: Query latency histograms (P50/P95/P99) for range buckets: <1d, 1-7d, 7-30d, >30d
Router resource metrics: CPU, memory, GC pauses during wide-range queries
Cost metrics: additional tokens and storage I/O introduced by prefetch
Per-tenant toggles and hint_aggressiveness value emitted in query traces
testing_plan: Unit tests for Index Hint Generator covering edge ranges and shard transitions
Integration tests simulating tenant-mix workloads (hot tenant, cold tenant, cross-tenant aggregations)
Chaos test: kill prefetch-daemon during active rollouts to validate graceful fallback
Load test: ramp wide-range query QPS and ensure router memory boundedness and no OOM
Regression job: nightly run comparing current branch against baseline for latency and cost
risks_mitigation: Risk: Prefetch can increase I/O and cost for low-value queries. Mitigation: require frequency threshold and cost-estimate check before prefetching
Risk: Index hints may be incorrect across schema changes. Mitigation: add planner versioning and schema-consistency checks; include fail-open behavior
Risk: Cross-tenant prefetch could surface tenant isolation concerns. Mitigation: store prefetch artifacts encrypted with per-tenant keys and enforce ACLs; provide opt-out per tenant
Risk: Increased operational complexity. Mitigation: feature-gated rollout, SLO guardrails, and detailed runbook

2026-03-08 Liam O'Connor: Added per-tenant flag in tenant-config API. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7543. Requesting design review from PM and Security.
